newsitem.title: UK: BT near three-year high after election.
newsitem.headline: BT near three-year high after election.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc moved within a whisker of a three-year high after good demand for paper, dealers said on Friday.
BT shares were up six pence, or 1.31 percent, to 462.5p by 1020 GMT in volume of 5.4 million while the FTSE-100 index was 5.9 points, or 0.13 percent, higher at 4,450.9.
"BT has benefited from the election. There is a feeling it is going to do well under Labour," a market maker at a British bank said.
Another marketmaker said: "There was a good market in it yesterday and again today". BT added 4p on Thursday.
Britain's Labour party won a landslide victory in Thursday's election, ousting the Conservatives from power after 18 years.
The Labour party said in April that if it won the election it would gradually lift restrictions on phone companies offering home entertainment services from 1998.
At the time BT welcomed the announcement in the Labour business manifesto but said it was too soon to say whether BT would offer television services.
On the flip side, Labour has pledged to levy a windfall tax on so-called excess profits made by privatised utilities, a collection of companies which may include BT.
